games.title: Animal Groups
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and name a variety of common animals including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals
games.instruction: Tap the group each animal belongs to.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about its skin, scales, feathers or fur, then try again.

questions.ask: A frog
A goldfish
A snake
A robin
A cow
A newt
A crocodile
A penguin

games.title: Material Match
games.skillName: Telling objects from the materials they are made of
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to distinguish between an object and the material from which it is made, and identify and name a variety of everyday materials, including wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, and rock
games.instruction: Tap the one that does not belong.
games.hint: Look again. Think about what each thing is made of.

questions.ask: Which one is a material, not an object?
Which one is an object, not a material?
Which one is NOT made of metal?
Which one is NOT made of glass?
Which one is NOT made of wood?
Which one is NOT made of rock?
Which one is NOT see-through?
Which one is NOT bendy?

games.title: Sense Check
games.skillName: Naming body parts and the sense each one helps with
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify, name, draw and label the basic parts of the human body and say which part of the body is associated with each sense
games.instruction: Is it true or false? Tap your answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Point to that part of your body and think about what it does.

questions.ask: You use your eyes to see.
You use your ears to taste.
You use your nose to smell.
Your tongue helps you hear.
You can feel things with your skin.
Your elbow is part of your leg.
Your knee is part of your leg.
Your toes are on your hands.

games.title: Who Eats What
games.skillName: Knowing what animals eat and how their bodies look
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and name a variety of common animals that are carnivores, herbivores and omnivores, and describe and compare the structure of a variety of common animals
games.instruction: Tap the word that fills the gap.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what the animal eats, or how its body helps it, then try again.

questions.ask: Cows eat grass. Cows are ___.
Lions eat meat. Lions are ___.
Foxes eat meat and berries. Foxes are ___.
Sharks eat fish and seals. Sharks are ___.
A herbivore eats only ___.
An omnivore eats plants and ___.
A fish uses its ___ to swim.
A bird's body is covered in ___.

games.title: Season Circle
games.skillName: Ordering the four seasons and their changes
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to observe changes across the four seasons, and observe and describe how day length varies
games.hint: Not quite. Think about which season comes after the last one shown, then try again.

questions.ask: Spring → Summer → Autumn → ?
Summer → Autumn → Winter → ?
Autumn → Winter → Spring → ?
Winter → Spring → Summer → ?
Bare tree in winter → Buds in spring → Green leaves in summer → ?
Short days in winter → Longer days in spring → ?
Long days in summer → Shorter days in autumn → ?
Hot summer → Cool autumn → ?

games.title: Plant Spotter
games.skillName: Naming common wild and garden plants and trees
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and name a variety of common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees
games.instruction: Listen to the clues and tap the plant.
games.hint: Not quite. Listen to the clues again and think about plants you have seen.

questions.ask: I am yellow. I grow on lawns. My seeds float away like fluff. What am I?
I am small with white petals and a yellow middle. I grow in grass. What am I?
I am a tall tree. I lose my leaves in autumn. My seeds are acorns. What am I?
I am an evergreen tree. My leaves are prickly and I have red berries. What am I?
I am an evergreen tree. I have thin green needles and cones. What am I?
I am a tree. I have blossom in spring and crunchy fruit in autumn. What am I?
I am a tall garden flower with a big yellow head full of seeds. What am I?
I am a blue wild flower shaped like a bell. I grow in woods in spring. What am I?

games.title: Material Tests
games.skillName: Predicting how materials behave from their properties
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe the simple physical properties of a variety of everyday materials
games.instruction: Tap what you think will happen.
games.hint: Think about the material. Is it hard or soft, bendy or stiff, waterproof or not?

questions.ask: What will happen if you drop a glass jar on a stone floor?
What will happen if you pour water on a paper towel?
What will happen if you pour water on a plastic sheet?
What will happen if you squeeze a sponge?
What will happen if you pull a rubber band?
What will happen if you put a wooden block in water?
What will happen if you put a metal key in water?
What will happen if you try to bend a stone with your hands?

games.title: Plant Parts
games.skillName: Naming the parts of flowering plants and trees
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and describe the basic structure of a variety of common flowering plants, including trees
games.hint: Not quite. Think about where that part is on a plant or tree.

questions.ask: The part under the soil that holds the plant in place
The thin stalk that holds up the flower and leaves
The flat green part of a plant
One of the coloured parts of a flower
The thick, woody stem of a tree
The part of a tree that grows out from the trunk
A tree that loses its leaves in autumn
A tree that keeps its leaves all year round

games.title: Weather Watch
games.skillName: Comparing weather and day length in each season
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to observe and describe weather associated with the seasons and how day length varies
games.hint: Not quite. Think about the weather and the daylight in each season.

questions.ask: Which season is usually the coldest?
Which season is usually the hottest?
Which season has the longest days?
Which season has the shortest days?
In which season are you most likely to see snow?
In which season do the most leaves fall from trees?
In which season do the most new buds and leaves appear?
Which month is usually the coldest in the UK?

games.title: Science Detectives
games.skillName: Choosing simple equipment and tests to find things out
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to observe closely using simple equipment, perform simple tests, identify and classify, and gather and record data to help in answering questions
games.instruction: Tap the best way to find out.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about which tool or test would help you find out, then try again.

questions.ask: What would you use to look closely at a tiny bug?
What would you use to find out how much rain fell?
What would you use to find out how hot it is outside?
What would you use to measure how tall a sunflower is?
How can you find out if a material is waterproof?
How can you find out which material is the bendiest?
You want to sort animals into groups. Which question helps?
How can you keep a record of the weather each day?
